newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs give up most gains but still end Tokyo firmer.
newsitem.headline: JGBs give up most gains but still end Tokyo firmer.

text.p: The benchmark September Japanese government bond futures contract surrendered most of the gains made in Tokyo on Monday as well as in overseas Friday trade, but still managed to close slightly higher.

Traders said there were few fresh factors they could put their fingers on to explain the slide, which emerged on the back of large-lot sales from several operators in late trade, but said they seemed to be at least partly due to natural corrections after sharp gains in Friday overseas trade.
Key September closed at 123.91, the day's low but still up 0.6 from Friday, with turnover a light 35,538 contracts.

Cash bonds, which had helped boost buying of futures for much of the day's trade, also gave up earlier gains. Yield on the key 10-year 182nd bond was at 2.380 percent as of 0612 GMT against 2.390 percent at Friday's Tokyo close after moving from 2.355 to 2.385 percent.

Tokyo stocks gained slightly in late trade and were likely to have put bonds under some downward pressure, although few traders gave this as a significant factor. The Nikkei closed up 152.72 at 20,681.07.
"What we were mostly seeing today was a lot of book-squaring, both buying and selling," one trader said.
September rose as high as 124.20 in mid-afternoon on sentiment carried over from Friday London trade, with additional upward impetus from strength in cash bonds, traders said.
Although the rise was made while steadily eroding offers, there were no strong factors behind the move, making JGBs vulnerable when heavy sales emerged in afternoon trade, they added.
"This increasing heavy topside then prompted loss-cut selling among operators who had bought in morning trade," a dealer at a city bank's securities arm said.
But he said support was likely to emerge around 123.80, an important technical point and also a point near where September had consolidated for some time last week.

"There also appear to be a number of institutional investors who still haven't bought much in the way of JGBs, and wherever their bids emerge is likely to become a short-term floor for the market," he added.

Little impact was detected from the release of economic indicators in afternoon trade. Some buying was sparked by the announcement that Japan's April industrial production fell a revised 0.5 percent from the previous month, but soon stopped.
Preliminary estimates had been for a 0.4 percent fall.

The announcement that May Tokyo department store sales were down 5.9 percent from a year earlier had virtually no impact, despite the fact that they were worse than the expected decline of 3.5 percent per year.
But rising feelings that the June 25 Bank of Japan (BOJ) "tankan" report will be weak are expected to prevent sharp losses in JGBs, traders said.
